THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Parmesan Corn Chex Snap Peas

Two-crunch side. 2 tbsp aged Parm + 4 tbsp crushed Corn Chex = the side that disappears off any plate.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME5 min prep + 20 min bake
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~80 cal | ~1g protein

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 2 cups fresh sugar snap peas, trimmed (~12 oz)
  • Olive oil spray (about 4 seconds total)
  • 2 tbsp Kirkland Parmigiano Reggiano Stravecchio, food-processed from a wedge to coarse grated

Ingredients — continued

  • 4 tbsp Corn Chex (General Mills), pulsed in food processor to coarse crumbs
  • Pinch salt + black pepper
  • Optional adult finish: cracked black pepper + lemon wedge at the table

You want a vegetable side that earns its own attention on the plate instead of being the leftover compartment. The crusted treatment turns snap peas into a craveable side — kids who reject 'plain peas' eat these because they read as 'crispy thing'.

Method

  1. 1.PREHEAT OVEN 425°F. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
  2. 2.PROCESS THE PARM. Cube ~2 oz of Kirkland Stravecchio. Pulse in a food processor until coarse grated (NOT fine — you want visible flecks). Set aside.
  3. 3.PULSE THE CHEX. 4 tbsp Corn Chex into the same processor. Pulse 4-5 times until coarse crumbs — about the texture of panko, NOT powder. Visible flake bits are the goal.
  4. 4.TOSS IN A BOWL. Snap peas + olive oil spray (2-3 sec) + 2 tbsp processed Parm + 4 tbsp crushed Chex + pinch salt + pepper. Toss until each pea is coated. Toss in the bowl FIRST, then spread on the pan — even adherence beats sprinkling on the sheet.
  5. 5.SPREAD ON PARCHMENT. Single layer. Crumbs that fall onto the parchment will crisp into clusters — bonus crunch.
  6. 6.BAKE 18-22 MIN. 425°F. Pull when the snap pea edges are deep golden + the crust is crispy. Some pods will char slightly — that's the texture target.
  7. 7.SERVE IMMEDIATELY. Best straight from the oven. They soften on standing.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid: Serve the kid portion as described above.

If something fails

Crumb fell off the peas: Not enough oil OR you didn't toss in a bowl first. Spray more (4 sec total), toss in a bowl, THEN spread. Crumbs adhere to the oil coating.

Peas turned mushy / didn't crisp: Oven not hot enough OR overcrowded sheet pan. 425°F + single layer is non-negotiable. If using 2 cups of peas, a half-sheet pan is the right size.

Crumb burned before peas crisped: Processor went too fine — fine crumb burns at high heat. Pulse 4-5 times max, leave visible flake bits. Or drop oven to 400°F + bake 25 min.

Too cheesy / overpowers the peas: You used MORE than 2 tbsp Parm. The 2:1 chex-to-Parm ratio is the brand — Parm adds salt + umami, Chex carries the crunch. Going heavier on Parm makes it dense and greasy.

Not enough crunch: Pulse Corn Chex less (more visible flake bits). Or bump to 5 tbsp. The crunch is what makes this side worth making vs plain roasted peas.

Kid won't eat them: Pull the most-charred pods for adults and serve the kid the lighter-browned ones. The visual matters more than the flavor at age 3-5.

Storage and reheating

Store: Best fresh. Day-2 peas soften in the fridge; the crust mostly survives but the snap pea pop is gone.

Reheat: Air fryer 400°F for 4-5 min. Restores ~70% of the original crispness. Oven 400°F for 6-8 min also works.

Lasts: 1 day fresh. 2-3 days if reheated dry-heat. Don't microwave — kills the crunch.

Estimated nutrition

~80 cal | ~1g protein.

Per-serving (~80 cal / 4g protein / 3g fat / 10g carbs / ~7g net) computed: 12 oz snap peas ÷ 4 = 3 oz/serving (~30 cal) + 0.5 tbsp Parm (~25 cal / 2g protein) + 1 tbsp crushed Chex (~30 cal) + oil spray (~5 cal). Net carbs lower because snap peas have ~3g fiber per serving. Flagged estimated because pea weight varies + Chex crush density varies.

Flavor target

Crispy golden edges on the snap peas + visible Parm + Chex crumb adhered to each pod. NOT mush, NOT bare. The chex gives bulk + crunch, the Parm gives salt + umami. Together the combo is dense enough to coat without weighing the peas down.

Adult plate | Kid plate

Adult plate

Adult

Full recipe as written. Optional finish: hit with cracked black pepper + a squeeze of lemon at the table.

Kid plate

Kid

Same recipe — kids eat the SAME crusted peas. The crust is a feature for kids (sweetness from peas + crunch). Some kids reject visible char on the pods; pull the ones that browned hardest for adults.

Brands I use

Kirkland Signature
Parmigiano Reggiano Stravecchio (aged over 36 months, ~2 lb wedge)
Real aged Parm with crystals + nutty depth that SURVIVE oven roasting. Pre-grated tubs disappear — you'd taste them as 'cheesy crumb' instead of 'aged Parm crunch'. Buy the wedge, process at home.
General Mills
Corn Chex Cereal (12 oz, gluten-free)
Pulsed to coarse crumbs = the crunch carrier. Gluten-free, neutral flavor, lighter than panko, more flavor than rice crisps. The 2:1 chex-to-Parm ratio is the move.
Chosen Foods
Avocado Oil Spray
Spray-not-pour. 2-3 second spray = enough oil for the crumb to adhere without drowning the peas in grease. Cross-recipe with id 38 Lettuce Wraps.
